subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept SQLite-backed sha256/size provenance as the trusted-host-read lifecycle for generated HTML after outbound staging?
rationale: The implementation is a well-tested bug fix, but it deliberately changes which staged local HTML can cross a host-read security boundary, which requires maintainer/security intent rather than automated cleanup.

options.title: Accept content-bound provenance
options.body: Land the PR after exact-head gates because the staged file is trusted only when it came from a trusted generated source and its bytes still match the recorded digest.

options.title: Request a tighter lifecycle
options.body: Ask the author to add additional bounds such as TTL pruning or chunked cleanup before merge if maintainers are not comfortable with the current table lifecycle.

options.title: Pause for security owner sign-off
options.body: Keep the PR open until a security owner explicitly approves or redirects the trust-boundary design.

recommendation.title: Accept content-bound provenance
recommendation.body: Land the PR after exact-head gates because the staged file is trusted only when it came from a trusted generated source and its bytes still match the recorded digest.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored and merged the original trusted generated HTML seam and has the strongest history signal for this security-boundary decision.
